claims.text: Multiphase Al-rich refractory high-entropy alloys with a B2 matrix will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The proposed non-monotonic transition is driven by competition between strengthening from local chemical order and embrittlement from long-range order.
The brittle minimum occurs at an intermediate degree of ordering where LRO impedes dislocation glide but transformation-mediated ductility is not yet active.
Al10Hf20Nb22Ti33V15 can have a single-phase ordered B2 initial state.
As-cast Al10Hf20Nb22Ti33V15 has approximately 33% LRO and 9% tensile strain.
Al0.5CoCrFeNi consists of an FCC matrix containing multicomponent NiAl-type B2 precipitates.

Aging between 650 K and 1000 K will progressively convert a random or locally ordered structure into a strongly long-range-ordered structure without significant phase separation or precipitate coarsening.
Aging must occur below the composition-specific order-disorder transformation temperature while remaining hot enough for atomic diffusion.
Increasing chemical order increases antiphase-boundary energy.
Low APBE and a relatively disordered B2 structure permit <111> dislocation glide and produce high ductility in Al-Hf-Nb-Ti-V alloys.
Development of LCO and LRO creates a rugged energy landscape that traps dislocations and causes embrittlement.
The B2 phase in Al0.5CoCrFeNi can undergo stress-induced martensitic transformation.
Prolonged aging of an Al-rich refractory B2 alloy can restore ductility by enabling SIMT or by lowering the effective APBE of particular slip systems.
Fracture strain versus aging time will follow a U- or V-shaped curve, with high initial ductility, an intermediate brittle minimum, and recovery at longer aging times.
The proposed transition occurs only when VEC lies outside a brittleness valley of 5.5 to 6.2.
A sufficiently multicomponent B2 phase can support SIMT.
The non-monotonic transition will not occur in single-phase random solid solutions that lack B2 ordering capability.
Conventional precipitation-strengthened alloys show a monotonic loss of ductility as aging continuously hardens and embrittles the matrix or precipitates.

contradictions.description: The target is described as a multiphase Al-RHEA, but the principal Al10Hf20Nb22Ti33V15 example is described as single-phase B2.
The hypothesis specifies a B2 matrix, whereas the alternative Al0.5CoCrFeNi system has an FCC matrix with B2 precipitates.
